transport: RJ-12 / RJ-25 (6P6C) modular jack · crossed-over (rolled-over) cable set, 5 m / 16.5 ft · discrete lines, no data bus · pinout AT THE INVERTER JACK (mirror of the remote's, per the vendor's own table): pin 1 = OVER TEMP LED, pin 2 = POWER ON LED, pin 3 = Vbattery, pin 4 = Ground/Common, pin 5 = Toggle, pin 6 = OVER LOAD LED
gotchas: CONTRADICTION with the retailer listing. The Quebec retailer offers the RC-15A alongside the PST-1500 as a "wired remote sold separately". Samlex's RC-15A manual lists compatibility as PST-600-12, PST-600-24, PST-1000-12 and PST-1000-24 only, and Samlex's PST landing page pairs RC-15A with PST-1000-12HD / PST-1000-F12

This is the only Samlex interface here with a full vendor pinout, and it is genuinely drivable by cabin-gpio: pull the Toggle line to command on/off, read the POWER ON line for switch-state. Vbattery and Ground are on the connector to power the panel.

What the manual does NOT state, and what a bench session must establish before any driver: the electrical behaviour of the four signal lines — drive level, polarity, active-high or active-low, source or sink, current limit, and whether Vbattery is raw pack voltage or regulated. The pin FUNCTIONS are vendor-documented;

The three LED lines are the inverter's own indicator drives, so reading them is passive; the Toggle line is the only output. `reports: switch-state` is what the map supports — whether the level shifter reads it cleanly is a bench question.
The inverter's own front-panel ON/OFF switch must be ON for the remote to do anything, and turning off from the remote still leaves control circuitry alive drawing current. Same caveat as the RC-300.
unmappedReports: Overload shutdown flag — a dedicated pin exists (pin 6 at the inverter jack) and MetricKind has no fault, alarm, or protection-status wire name to carry it. This is a real contract gap: the wire is right there and there is nowhere to put it., Over-temperature shutdown flag — dedicated pin (pin 1 at the inverter jack), same gap.
